title: Architecting a two-sided marketplace: lessons from Uzhavan Rentals
summary: Notes on role-scoping with Google OAuth and JWT, and what broke first when both sides of the marketplace could act on the same data.

blocks.text: A two-sided marketplace like Uzhavan Rentals involves two distinct profiles: equipment owners looking to rent out machinery, and local farmers looking to rent it. Securing their interactions requires strict boundary controls. I implemented authentication using Google OAuth, linking identity validation with database user records.

Once identified, the system issues a JSON Web Token (JWT) containing scoped role payloads (e.g. 'role: owner' or 'role: renter'). Routes are guarded by custom middleware that decodes this token and grants access only if the payload matches the route permissions.

One of the earliest architectural bottlenecks arose from concurrent data modifications. In a marketplace, multiple renters can request the same tractor for the same dates, while the owner is in the process of approving another request. Without atomic controls, this leads to double bookings and inconsistent states.

To solve this, I designed a strict booking state machine. When an owner approves a booking, the system runs an atomic transaction: it updates the status of the chosen booking to 'approved' and rejects all other overlapping pending requests in a single database operation.

Exposing public-facing endpoints for bookings makes the platform vulnerable to scraping and automated spam. Protecting backend routes involved combining network-level constraints and HTTP header hygiene.
I set up Express Rate Limit to restrict request frequencies on sensitive endpoints, alongside Helmet to enforce strict secure transport policies and prevent cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks.

items: Express Rate Limit: Limit login and checkout API hits to 5 requests per minute.
Helmet Headers: Disable HTTP headers like 'X-Powered-By' to hide server technologies.
CORS Config: Restrict request origins strictly to the authorized client domains.
